key_facts: On November 1, 2024, CHP Officers Meza-Gonzalez and Melano contacted Plaintiff on the I-580 East shoulder in Livermore (CHP Case RJ68845). The DS-367 chemical-test-refusal designation and Arrest Report triggered DMV APS Case 34739340. After a January 24, 2025 Microsoft Teams hearing, Hearing Officer Diana Candelaria issued a February 11, 2025 Decision sustaining a one-year Class A CDL suspension (Feb. 20, 2025 – Feb. 19, 2026) without addressing the November 5, 2024 PC § 849(b)(1) Detention Certificate. Matter 7 (federal §1983, 2:26-cv-00983-DC-CSK) and Matter 8 (state mandate, 26WM000135, abandoned) litigate that APS outcome. This matter consolidates the underlying incident/APS evidence and both Candelaria docket PDF sets under one owning folder. Plaintiff signed an operative N.D. Cal. Complaint (v3, 47 pp.) and print intake packet against Candelaria (individual) and Gordon (official capacity) on Aug. 7, 2026, expressly alleging that the prior E.D. Cal. Matter 7 action arising from the same Nov. 1, 2024 incident was voluntarily dismissed without prejudice. The court docketed it as Dkt. 1 on Aug. 10, 2026, and a 44-page First Amended Complaint has since superseded it. The FAC pleads that Plaintiff's SR-22 filing under Vehicle Code § 16430 became effective May 18, 2026 — a Dairyland/Viking non-owner policy at $281.28 per year — so the three-year maintenance period runs through approximately May 2029; Matter 32's ¶36(d) now states the same end date for the same obligation. Drafts v1 (47 pp.) and v2 (15 pp. short-form) retained.
procedural_status: Opened August 7, 2026 as Matter 33 to hold the Candelaria / DMV APS slice of the CHP cluster: six Nov. 1 incident and APS discovery PDFs plus the Centerline wage reference in matter-33/incident/; twelve Matter 7 federal PDFs in matter-33/from-07/; six Matter 8 mandamus PDFs in matter-33/from-08/; and the June 15, 2026 Candelaria F&R in matter-33/opinions/. Matters 1, 2, 7, 8 and 32 cross-reference those paths. The N.D. Cal. complaint was signed Aug. 7 and docketed Aug. 10, 2026 as No. 3:26-cv-08272-LJC, assigned to Magistrate Judge Lisa J. Cisneros in San Francisco; the clerk's intake stamp shows the San Jose office. Four documents are on the docket: complaint (Dkt. 1), summonses as to both defendants (Dkt. 2), Plaintiff's magistrate-jurisdiction election consenting under 28 U.S.C. § 636(c) (Dkt. 3), and the court's order setting the initial case management conference and ADR deadlines (Dkt. 4). Both summonses are addressed to the defendants care of the DMV Legal Affairs Division, Mail Station C128, 2415 First Avenue, Sacramento, CA 95818. A First Amended Complaint (44 pp.) now supersedes Dkt. 1: it carries the assigned case number in the caption, pleads the SR-22 maintenance period from the May 18, 2026 filing date through approximately May 2029, and drops the fabricated Burrell v. Jackson passage. Because neither defendant has been served, Rule 15(a)(1)(A) still allows amendment as of course, so no leave is required. The FAC is generated from internal/scripts/matter33-ndcal-fac.py — edit that script and re-run rather than hand-patching the PDF. Open items: the Civil L.R. 3-15 certification of conflicts and interested entities was due with Plaintiff's first appearance and is not on the docket; Dkt. 4 requires that order and the Civil L.R. 4-2 supplementary material to be served with the operative pleading; the § 636(c) consent binds only Plaintiff until both defendants consent, and a single declination reassigns the case to a district judge; the FAC still identifies the related Meza-Gonzalez action by caption only, so its case number must be inserted at ¶¶ 8, 14, 31 and 88 once assigned; and the representation that Matter 7 was voluntarily dismissed without prejudice still needs confirming on the E.D. Cal. docket. Related case listed on the JS-44: Serrato 4:26-cv-05953-ASK. Dated deadlines live in timeline.json.
damages: The Dkt. 1 complaint seeks compensatory damages exceeding $214,000, punitive damages of at least $100,000, JS-44 demand alignment $250,000 (min.), vacatur of APS Case 34739340, SR-22 relief, CDL-record expungement, and structural APS reform. Matter 33 also remains documentary owner of the Matter 7/8 PDF sets (no separate damages under the document-home role).
risk: Refiled in N.D. Cal. after the alleged Matter 7 E.D. Cal. voluntary dismissal — confirm that dismissal is actually on the E.D. Cal. docket, since Dkt. 1 represents it to this court; watch claim-preclusion and forum-shopping arguments. Service is the near-term exposure: nothing is served, Rule 4(m) expires Nov. 8, 2026 (four days before the initial conference), and both defendants must be reached through DMV Legal Affairs in Sacramento. Consenting to magistrate jurisdiction gives up the district-judge review layer that produced the Matter 7 objections track, and is ineffective unless both defendants also consent. Dkt. 1 carries a known-fabricated authority at page 43: Burrell v. Jackson, 2003 WL 23545858, which the citation ledger records as NOT_FOUND. A nonexistent case cannot be distinguished, and the defendants would brief quasi-judicial immunity straight at that passage. The First Amended Complaint cures it — neither Burrell nor its companion cite (Baker v. Bzdyra, 2019 WL 6619348, misspelled 'Bzydra' in Dkt. 1) appears anywhere in the FAC — so lodging the FAC is the remediation vehicle and no errata is needed. Until the FAC is accepted, Dkt. 1 remains the pleading of record and the citation debt entry stands. Coordinate with the Matter 32 Meza-Gonzalez N.D. Cal. companion, whose case number is still unrecorded in the portfolio, and the Serrato related-case notice. Path updates for Matters 1/2/7/8/32 already point at /documents/matter-33/ for the historical PDF set.
